answer: A harbor for agent work can resist sybils by requiring each new identity to post a slashable bond before taking paid jobs, like a lantern that only stays lit while fuel remains. The bond is locked and forfeited on proven fraud, so each fake identity adds real capital cost, not just compute. Reputation then grows slowly, like cedar, from verified work: newcomers start with small tasks and gain larger limits only after honest attestations. An attacker must therefore fund and age many identities at once, making a large sybil fleet expensive and slow.
